title.zh: 卷二十五 志第六: 地理中 南京路 河北東路 河北西路 山東東路 山東西路
title.en: Volume 25 Treatises 6: Geography 2 - Nanjing Circuit, Hebei Circuit East, Hebei Circuit West, Shandong Circuit East, Shandong Circuit West
title.raw: 卷二十五 志第六: 地理中 南京路 河北東路 河北西路 山東東路 山東西路 Volume 25 Treatises 6: Geography 2 - Nanjing Circuit, Hebei Circuit East, Hebei Circuit West, Shandong Circuit East, Shandong Circuit West

translations.literal: Nanjing Circuit
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing Circuit

sentences.zh: 南京路，國初曰汴京，貞元元年更號南京。

translations.literal: Nanjing Circuit—in the founding era called Bianjing; in Zhenyuan 1 renamed Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing Circuit was called Bianjing at the founding; in Zhenyuan 1 it became Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 府三，領節鎮三，防禦八，刺史郡八，縣一百五。

translations.literal: Three prefectures, commanding three jiedushi posts, eight defense commanderies, eight cishi commanderies, one hundred five counties.
translations.idiomatic: It had three prefectures, three jiedushi posts, eight defense commanderies, eight cishi commanderies, and 105 counties.

sentences.zh: 都城門十四，曰開陽，曰宣仁，曰安利，曰平化。

translations.literal: The capital had fourteen gates, named Kaiyang, Xuanren, Anli, and Pinghua.
translations.idiomatic: The capital had fourteen gates: Kaiyang, Xuanren, Anli, and Pinghua.

sentences.zh: 曰通遠，曰宜照，曰利川，曰崇德，曰迎秋，曰廣澤，曰順義，曰迎朔，曰順常，曰廣智。

translations.literal: Named Tongyuan, Yizhao, Lichuan, Chongde, Yingqiu, Guangze, Shunyi, Yingshuo, Shunchang, and Guangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Also Tongyuan, Yizhao, Lichuan, Chongde, Yingqiu, Guangze, Shunyi, Yingshuo, Shunchang, and Guangzhi.

sentences.zh: 宮城門，南外門曰南薰，南薰北新城門曰豐宜，橋曰龍津橋，北門曰丹鳳，其門三。

translations.literal: Palace gates: the outer south gate Nanxun; north of Nanxun the new-city gate Fengyi; the bridge Longjin Bridge; the north gate Danfeng—three gates.
translations.idiomatic: Palace gates: outer south Nanxun; north of Nanxun, new-city Fengyi; Longjin Bridge; north Danfeng with three openings.

sentences.zh: 丹鳳北曰舟橋，橋少北曰文武樓，遵禦路而北橫街也。

translations.literal: North of Danfeng was Zhou Bridge; a little north of the bridge Wuwu Tower—the north cross-street along the imperial road.
translations.idiomatic: North of Danfeng stood Zhou Bridge; just north, Wuwu Tower marked the north cross-street on the imperial avenue.

sentences.zh: 東曰太廟，西曰郊社，正北曰承天門，其門五，雙闕前引，東曰登聞檢院，西曰登聞鼓院。

translations.literal: East: Grand Temple; west: suburban altar; due north Chengtian Gate—five gates, twin towers ahead; east Dengwen Inspection Court; west Dengwen Drum Court.
translations.idiomatic: East lay the Grand Temple, west the suburban altar; due north Chengtian Gate with five openings and twin towers; east the Dengwen Inspection Court, west the Dengwen Drum Court.

sentences.zh: 檢院東曰左掖門，門南曰待漏院。

translations.literal: East of the Inspection Court Left Yeye Gate; south of the gate the Dawn-Watch Court.
translations.idiomatic: East of the inspection court was Left Yeye Gate; south of it, the Dawn-Watch Court.

sentences.zh: 鼓院西曰右掖門，門南曰都堂。

translations.literal: West of the Drum Court Right Yeye Gate; south of the gate the Chief Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: West of the drum court was Right Yeye Gate; south of it, the Chief Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 直承天門北曰大慶門，門東曰日精門，又東曰左升平門。

translations.literal: Due north of Chengtian Gate Daqing Gate; east of the gate Rijing Gate; further east Left Shengping Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Straight north of Chengtian Gate stood Daqing Gate; east of it Rijing Gate, and farther east Left Shengping Gate.

sentences.zh: 大慶門西曰月華門，又西曰右升平門。

translations.literal: West of Daqing Gate Yuehua Gate; further west Right Shengping Gate.
translations.idiomatic: West of Daqing Gate was Yuehua Gate, and farther west Right Shengping Gate.

sentences.zh: 正殿曰大慶殿，前有龍墀，又南有丹墀，又南曰沙墀，東廡曰嘉福樓，西廡曰嘉瑞樓。

translations.literal: The main hall Daqing Hall; before it the dragon terrace; farther south the cinnabar terrace; farther south the sand terrace; east wing Jiafu Tower; west wing Jiarui Tower.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall was Daqing Hall, with dragon terrace before it, cinnabar terrace south, sand terrace farther south, Jiafu Tower on the east wing and Jiarui on the west.

translations.literal: Behind Daqing was Deyi Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Behind Daqing stood Deyi Hall.

sentences.zh: 殿東曰左升龍門，西曰右升龍門。

translations.literal: East of the hall Left Ascending Dragon Gate; west Right Ascending Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: East of the hall was Left Ascending Dragon Gate; west, Right Ascending Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 正門曰隆德，內有隆德殿，有蕭牆，有丹墀。

translations.literal: The main gate Longde; within Longde Hall, a screen wall, and a cinnabar terrace.
translations.idiomatic: The main gate was Longde; inside were Longde Hall, a screen wall, and a cinnabar terrace.

sentences.zh: 隆德殿左曰東上閣門，右曰西上閣門，皆南向。

translations.literal: Left of Longde Hall East Upper Pavilion Gate; right West Upper Pavilion Gate—both facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Left of Longde Hall was East Upper Pavilion Gate; right, West Upper Pavilion Gate—both south-facing.

translations.literal: The drum tower in the east; the bell tower in the west.
translations.idiomatic: The drum tower stood east; the bell tower west.

sentences.zh: 隆德之次曰仁安門、仁安殿，東則內侍局，又東曰近侍局，又東則嚴祗門，宮中則稱曰撒合門，少南曰東樓，則授除樓也。

translations.literal: Next after Longde Ren’an Gate and Ren’an Hall; east the Inner Service Bureau; farther east the Close Attendants Bureau; farther east Yanqi Gate—in the palace called Sahe Gate; a little south East Tower, the appointment tower.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Longde were Ren’an Gate and Ren’an Hall; east lay the Inner Service Bureau, then the Close Attendants Bureau, then Yanqi Gate (called Sahe Gate within the palace); a little south, East Tower for appointments.

translations.literal: West West Tower.
translations.idiomatic: To the west was West Tower.

sentences.zh: 仁安之次曰純和殿，正寢也。

translations.literal: Next after Ren’an Chunhe Hall—the principal sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Ren’an was Chunhe Hall, the principal sleeping quarters.

sentences.zh: 純和西曰雪香亭，亭北則後妃位也，有樓，樓西曰瓊香亭，亭西曰涼位，有樓，樓北少西曰玉清殿。

translations.literal: West of Chunhe Snow-Fragrance Pavilion; north of the pavilion the empresses’ quarters, with a tower; west of the tower Qiong-Fragrance Pavilion; west of the pavilion the Cool Quarters, with a tower; a little northwest of the tower Yuqing Hall.
translations.idiomatic: West of Chunhe stood Snow-Fragrance Pavilion; north of it the empresses’ quarters with a tower; west, Qiong-Fragrance Pavilion; west again the Cool Quarters with a tower; northwest of that tower, Yuqing Hall.

sentences.zh: 純和之次曰福寧殿，殿后曰苑門，內曰仁智殿，有二太湖石，左曰敷錫神運萬歲峰，右曰玉京獨秀太平岩，殿曰山莊，其西南曰翠微閣。

translations.literal: Next after Chunhe Funing Hall; behind the hall Garden Gate; within, Renzhi Hall with two Taihu rocks—left “Bestowed Divine Transport Ten-Thousand-Year Peak,” right “Jade Capital Unique Beauty Peaceful Rock”; the hall called Mountain Villa; southwest Cuwei Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond Chunhe was Funing Hall; behind it Garden Gate led within to Renzhi Hall with two Taihu rocks—left inscribed “Bestowed Divine Transport Ten-Thousand-Year Peak,” right “Jade Capital Unique Beauty Peaceful Rock”—and the hall called Mountain Villa; southwest stood Cuwei Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 苑門東曰仙韶院，院北曰翠峰，峰之洞曰大滌湧翠，東連長生殿，又東曰湧金殿，又東曰蓬萊殿。

translations.literal: East of Garden Gate Xianzhao Court; north of the court Emerald Peak; the peak’s cave Great Purge Surging Emerald; east linked Longevity Hall; farther east Surging Gold Hall; farther east Penglai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: East of Garden Gate was Xianzhao Court; north, Emerald Peak with cave Great Purge Surging Emerald; east connected Longevity Hall, then Surging Gold Hall, then Penglai Hall.

sentences.zh: 長生西曰浮玉殿，又西曰瀛洲殿。

translations.literal: West of Longevity Floating Jade Hall; farther west Yingzhou Hall.
translations.idiomatic: West of Longevity stood Floating Jade Hall, then Yingzhou Hall.

sentences.zh: 長生殿南曰閱武殿，又南曰內藏庫。

translations.literal: South of Longevity Hall Review Troops Hall; farther south Inner Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: South of Longevity Hall was Review Troops Hall, then the Inner Treasury.

sentences.zh: 嚴祗門東曰尚食局，又東曰宣徽院，院北曰禦藥院，又北右藏庫，東則左藏庫。

translations.literal: East of Yanqi Gate Imperial Kitchen Bureau; farther east Xuanhui Court; north of the court Imperial Pharmacy; farther north Right Treasury; east the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: East of Yanqi Gate was the Imperial Kitchen Bureau, then Xuanhui Court; north of the court, Imperial Pharmacy; farther north Right Treasury, with Left Treasury to the east.

sentences.zh: 宣徽院東曰點檢司，司北曰秘書監，又北曰學士院，又北曰諫院，又北曰武器署。

translations.literal: East of Xuanhui Court Inspection Office; north of the office Secretariat; farther north Hanlin Academy; farther north Remonstrance Court; farther north Weapons Office.
translations.idiomatic: East of Xuanhui Court was the Inspection Office; north, the Secretariat; farther north Hanlin Academy, Remonstrance Court, and Weapons Office.

sentences.zh: 點檢司南曰儀鸞局，又南曰尚輦局。

translations.literal: South of the Inspection Office Ceremonial Escort Bureau; farther south Imperial Carriage Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Inspection Office stood Ceremonial Escort Bureau, then Imperial Carriage Bureau.

sentences.zh: 宣徽院南曰拱衛司，又南曰尚衣局。

translations.literal: South of Xuanhui Court Arch Guard Office; farther south Imperial Wardrobe Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: South of Xuanhui Court was Arch Guard Office, then Imperial Wardrobe Bureau.

sentences.zh: 其南為繁禧門，又南安泰門，門與左升龍門相直。

translations.literal: South of that Fanxi Gate; farther south Antai Gate—the gate aligned with Left Ascending Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Farther south stood Fanxi Gate, then Antai Gate, aligned with Left Ascending Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 東則壽聖宮，兩宮太后位也，本明俊殿，試進士之所。

translations.literal: East Shousheng Palace—residence of the two empress dowagers; originally Mingjun Hall, where civil-service examinees were tested.
translations.idiomatic: To the east was Shousheng Palace, seat of the two empress dowagers; it had been Mingjun Hall, venue for civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 宮北曰徽音院，又北燕壽殿，殿垣後少西曰振肅衛司，東曰中衛尉司。

translations.literal: North of the palace Huiyin Court; farther north Yanshou Hall; a little west behind the hall wall Zhensu Guard Office; east Central Guard Office.
translations.idiomatic: North of the palace lay Huiyin Court, then Yanshou Hall; a little west behind its wall, Zhensu Guard Office; east, Central Guard Office.

sentences.zh: 儀鸞局東曰小東華門，更漏在焉。

translations.literal: East of the Ceremonial Escort Bureau Small Donghua Gate—where the clepsydra stood.
translations.idiomatic: East of Ceremonial Escort Bureau was Small Donghua Gate, site of the water clock.

sentences.zh: 中衛尉司東曰祗肅門，少東南曰將軍司。

translations.literal: East of the Central Guard Office Zhisu Gate; a little southeast General’s Office.
translations.idiomatic: East of Central Guard Office was Zhisu Gate; a little southeast, General’s Office.

sentences.zh: 徽音、壽聖東曰太后苑，苑殿曰慶春，與燕壽殿並。

translations.literal: East of Huiyin and Shousheng the Empress Dowager Garden; garden hall Qingchun, alongside Yanshou Hall.
translations.idiomatic: East of Huiyin and Shousheng lay the Empress Dowager Garden; its hall Qingchun stood beside Yanshou Hall.

translations.literal: Small Donghua faced the main Donghua Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Small Donghua faced the main Donghua Gate.

sentences.zh: 東華門內正北尚廄局，其西北曰臨武殿。

translations.literal: Within Donghua Gate due north Imperial Stables; northwest Linwu Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Donghua Gate, due north Imperial Stables; northwest Linwu Hall.

sentences.zh: 左掖門北，尚食局南曰宮苑司。

translations.literal: North of Left Yeye Gate, south of Imperial Kitchen Bureau—Palace Parks Office.
translations.idiomatic: North of Left Yeye Gate and south of Imperial Kitchen Bureau stood Palace Parks Office.

translations.literal: Northwest Imperial Brewery and Hot-Medicine Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest were Imperial Brewery and Hot-Medicine Bureau.

sentences.zh: 侍儀司少西曰府寶局、器物局，又西則撒合門也。

translations.literal: A little west of Ceremonial Protocol Office Treasury Bureau and Objects Bureau; farther west again Sahe Gate.
translations.idiomatic: A little west of Ceremonial Protocol Office were Treasury Bureau and Objects Bureau; farther west again Sahe Gate.

sentences.zh: 嘉瑞樓西曰三廟，正殿曰德昌，東曰文昭，西曰光興。

translations.literal: West of Jiarui Tower the Three Temples; main hall Dechang; east Wenzhao; west Guangxing.
translations.idiomatic: West of Jiarui Tower stood the Three Temples: main hall Dechang, east Wenzhao, west Guangxing.

translations.literal: Behind Dechang—the Xuanzong temple.
translations.idiomatic: Behind Dechang lay Xuanzong’s temple.

sentences.zh: 宮西門曰西華，與東華相直，北門曰安 貞。

translations.literal: The palace west gate Xihua, aligned with Donghua; north gate An  Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The palace west gate was Xihua, opposite Donghua; the north gate An  Zhen.

translations.literal: Kaifeng Prefecture, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng Prefecture, upper grade.

sentences.zh: 留守司留守帶本府尹，兼本路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: The resident commissioner also held this prefecture’s governorship and was overall commander of the circuit’s troops.
translations.idiomatic: The resident commissioner doubled as prefect and as overall commander of circuit forces.

sentences.zh: 天德二年罷行台尚書省，置轉運司、提刑司。

translations.literal: In Tiande 2 the traveling Secretariat was abolished and transport and judicial offices were set.
translations.idiomatic: Tiande 2 abolished the traveling Secretariat and established transport and judicial offices.

translations.literal: In Tiande 2 a commandery general’s office was set.
translations.idiomatic: Tiande 2 also established a commandery general’s office.

translations.literal: There were four medicine markets and a monopoly market.
translations.idiomatic: It had four medicine markets and a monopoly market.

sentences.zh: 產蜜蠟、香茶、心紅、硃紅、地龍、黃柏。

translations.literal: Products: beeswax, fragrant tea, heart-red, cinnabar-red, earthworm, and yellow cypress.
translations.idiomatic: Local products included beeswax, fragrant tea, heart-red dye, cinnabar-red, earthworms, and yellow cypress.

sentences.zh: 天德四年，戶二十三萬五千八百九十。

translations.literal: Tiande 4, households two hundred thirty-five thousand eight hundred ninety.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 4, households: 235,890.

sentences.zh: 泰和末，戶百七十四萬六千二百一十。

translations.literal: At Taihe’s end, households one million seven hundred forty-six thousand two hundred ten.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Taihe, households: 1,746,210.

translations.literal: Fifteen counties, fifteen towns:
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen counties and fifteen towns:

translations.literal: Kaifeng east attached to the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng east, attached to the seat.

translations.literal: There were the old Tongjin ford, Lin’ai Pass, and the Bian Canal.
translations.idiomatic: It had the old Tongjin ford, Lin’ai Pass, and the Bian Canal.

translations.literal: One town: Yanjia.
translations.idiomatic: One town: Yanjia.

translations.literal: Xiangfu west attached to the prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangfu west, attached to the seat.

sentences.zh: 有岳台、浚水、沙台、崇台、夷門山、蔡河、金水河、廣濟河、寒泉河。

translations.literal: There were Yue Terrace, Jun River, Shatai, Chong Terrace, Yimen Mountain, Cai River, Jinshui River, Guangji River, and Hanquan River.
translations.idiomatic: It had Yue Terrace, Jun River, Shatai, Chong Terrace, Yimen Mountain, Cai River, Jinshui, Guangji River, and Hanquan River.

translations.literal: Three towns: Chenqiao, Bajiao, and Guoqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Three towns: Chenqiao, Bajiao, and Guoqiao.

translations.literal: Yangwu had Shachi Pool and Heiyang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Yangwu had Shachi Pool and Heiyang Mountain.

translations.literal: Yellow River, Bian Canal, and Baigou River.
translations.idiomatic: It had the Yellow River, Bian Canal, and Baigou River.

sentences.zh: 通許宋名咸平，大定二十九年以與咸平府重，更。

translations.literal: Tongxu—Song name Xianping; in the twenty-ninth year of Dading renamed because it duplicated Xianping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tongxu, called Xianping under the Song, was renamed in Dading 29 to avoid clashing with Xianping Prefecture.

translations.literal: There were Niushou walled town and Qiuting.
translations.idiomatic: It had Niushou walled town and Qiuting.

sentences.zh: 泰康有魯溝、蔡河、渦河、鎮一崔橋。

translations.literal: Taikang had Lugou, Cai River, Wo River; one town: Cuiqiao.
translations.idiomatic: Taikang had Lugou, Cai River, and Wo River; one town: Cuiqiao.

sentences.zh: 中牟有汴河、鄭河、中牟台。

translations.literal: Zhongmu had Bian Canal, Zheng River, and Zhongmu Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongmu had the Bian Canal, Zheng River, and Zhongmu Terrace.

sentences.zh: 鎮四圃田、陽武、萬勝、白沙鎮。

translations.literal: Four towns: Putian, Yangwu, Wansheng, and Baisha.
translations.idiomatic: Four towns: Putian, Yangwu, Wansheng, and Baisha.

sentences.zh: 杞宋雍丘縣，杞國也，正隆後更今名。

translations.literal: Qi—Song Yongqiu county, land of the Qi state; after Zhenglong renamed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was Song Yongqiu county, ancient Qi state; after Zhenglong it took the present name.

translations.literal: One town: Yucheng.
translations.idiomatic: One town: Yucheng.

sentences.zh: 鄢陵有洧水、潩水、太丘城。

translations.literal: Yanling had Wei River, Yi River, and Taiqiu walled town.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling had the Wei, Yi, and Taiqiu walled town.

translations.literal: One town: Malan Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: One town: Malan Bridge.

translations.literal: Weishi had Huimin Canal and Changming Ditch.
translations.idiomatic: Weishi had Huimin Canal and Changming Ditch.

translations.literal: Two towns: Zhujia Bend and Songlou.
translations.idiomatic: Two towns: Zhujia Bend and Songlou.

sentences.zh: 扶溝有祁耶山、洧水、白亭。

translations.literal: Fugou had Qiye Mountain, Wei River, and Baiting.
translations.idiomatic: Fugou had Qiye Mountain, Wei River, and Baiting.

translations.literal: Two towns: Jianxiong and Yidian.
translations.idiomatic: Two towns: Jianxiong and Yidian.

translations.literal: Formerly there was Chicang town.
translations.idiomatic: It formerly had Chicang town.

sentences.zh: 陳留有皇柏山、狼丘、汴河。

translations.literal: Chenliu had Huangbai Mountain, Lang Hill, and Bian Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Chenliu had Huangbai Mountain, Lang Hill, and the Bian Canal.

sentences.zh: 延津貞祐三年七月升為延州。

translations.literal: Yanzhou—in the seventh month of Zhenyou 3 raised to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou was promoted to Yan Prefecture in the seventh month of Zhenyou 3.

translations.literal: There were Tushan and Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: It had Tushan and the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 洧川貞祐二年置惠民倉，興定二年四月以尉氏縣之宋樓鎮升。

translations.literal: Weichuan—in Zhenyou 2 Huimin granary was set; in the fourth month of Xingding 2 raised from Weishi county’s Songlou town.
translations.idiomatic: Weichuan: Huimin granary was set in Zhenyou 2; in the fourth month of Xingding 2 it was raised from Weishi’s Songlou town.

translations.literal: Suizhou, lower grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Suizhou, lower grade, with a cishi.

sentences.zh: 宋拱州保慶軍，國初猶稱拱州，天德三年更。

translations.literal: Song Gongzhou Baojing Army; at the founding still called Gongzhou; changed in Tiande 3.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song it was Gongzhou’s Baojing Army; at the founding it was still Gongzhou; renamed in Tiande 3.

translations.literal: Households forty-six thousand three hundred sixty.
translations.idiomatic: Households: 46,360.

translations.literal: Three counties, one town:
translations.idiomatic: Three counties and one town:

translations.literal: Xiangyi—ancient Xiang and Niu lands.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyi lay on ancient Xiang and Niu territory.

sentences.zh: 有汴河、睢水、渙水、承匡城。

translations.literal: There were Bian Canal, Sui River, Huan River, and Chengkong walled town.
translations.idiomatic: It had the Bian Canal, Sui, Huan, and Chengkong walled town.

translations.literal: One town: Chonghua.
translations.idiomatic: One town: Chonghua.

sentences.zh: 考城宋隸東京，正隆前隸曹州，後來屬。

translations.literal: Kaocheng—under the Song subordinate to Dongjing; before Zhenglong subordinate to Caozhou; later came under this circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Kaocheng was under Song Dongjing; before Zhenglong it belonged to Caozhou; later it was transferred here.

sentences.zh: 有葵丘、黃河、黃陵岡，元光二年改為通安堡。

translations.literal: There were Kui Hill, Yellow River, and Huangling Mound; in Yuanguang 2 renamed Tong’an Fort.
translations.idiomatic: It had Kui Hill, the Yellow River, and Huangling Mound; in Yuanguang 2 it became Tong’an Fort.

sentences.zh: 柘城古株林，首止地在焉。

translations.literal: Zhecheng—ancient Zhulin; the Shouzhi site was there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhecheng was ancient Zhulin; the Shouzhi site lay there.

translations.literal: There were Huan River, Pao River, and Hong River.
translations.idiomatic: It had the Huan, Pao, and Hong rivers.

sentences.zh: 本泰安軍，大定二十二年升。

translations.literal: Originally Tai’an Army; promoted in the twenty-second year of Dading.
translations.idiomatic: It had been Tai’an Army, promoted in Dading 22.

sentences.zh: 戶三萬一千四百三十五。

translations.literal: Households thirty-one thousand four hundred thirty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Households: 31,435.

translations.literal: Three counties, two towns:
translations.idiomatic: Three counties, two towns:

translations.literal: Fengfu yi.
translations.idiomatic: Fengfu, the prefectural seat county.

sentences.zh: 有泰山，社首山、龜山、徂徠山、亭亭山。

translations.literal: There are Mount Tai, Mount Sheshou, Mount Gui, Mount Culai, and Mount Tingting.
translations.idiomatic: It had Mount Tai, Mount Sheshou, Mount Gui, Mount Culai, and Mount Tingting.

translations.literal: There are Wen River and Liang River.
translations.idiomatic: It had the Wen River and the Liang River.

translations.literal: Two towns: Taiping, Jingfeng.
translations.idiomatic: Two towns: Taiping and Jingfeng.

sentences.zh: 萊蕪有肅然山、安期山、贏汶水、牟汶水。

translations.literal: Laiwu had Mount Suran, Mount Anqi, Yingwen River, and Mouwen River.
translations.idiomatic: Laiwu had Mount Suran, Mount Anqi, the Yingwen River, and the Mouwen River.

translations.literal: Dezhou, upper grade, defense commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhou, upper grade, a defense commandery.

translations.literal: Song Pingyuan commandery army.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song it was Pingyuan commandery army.

translations.literal: Households fifteen thousand fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Households: 15,053.

translations.literal: Three counties, seven towns:
translations.idiomatic: Three counties, seven towns:

translations.literal: Ande had Gejin River.
translations.idiomatic: Ande had the Gejin River.

sentences.zh: 鎮四磁博、向化、盤河、德安。

translations.literal: Four towns: Cibo, Xianghua, Panhe, De’an.
translations.idiomatic: Four towns: Cibo, Xianghua, Panhe, and De’an.

translations.literal: Pingyuan had the Jin River.
translations.idiomatic: Pingyuan had the Jin River.

translations.literal: One town: Shuiwu.
translations.idiomatic: One town: Shuiwu.

translations.literal: Deping: two towns—Huairen, Kong Family Market.
translations.idiomatic: Deping had two towns: Huairen and Kong Family Market.

translations.literal: Caozhou, middle grade, cishi.
translations.idiomatic: Caozhou, middle grade, with a cishi.

sentences.zh: 宋興仁府濟陰郡彰信軍。

translations.literal: Song Xingren Prefecture, Jiyin commandery, Zhangxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song it was Xingren Prefecture, Jiyin commandery, Zhangxin Army.

sentences.zh: 本隸南京，泰和八年來屬。

translations.literal: Originally subordinate to Nanjing; in the eighth year of Taihe it came under this route.
translations.idiomatic: It had been under Nanjing; Taihe 8 it was placed under Shandong West Route.

sentences.zh: 大定八年城為河所沒，遷州治于古乘氏縣。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dading the city was destroyed by the river; the prefectural seat moved to the old Chenshi county.
translations.idiomatic: Dading 8 a flood destroyed the city and the seat moved to the site of ancient Chenshi county.

sentences.zh: 戶一萬二千六百七十七。

translations.literal: Households twelve thousand six hundred seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Households: 12,677.

translations.literal: Three counties, one town:
translations.idiomatic: Three counties, one town:

translations.literal: Jiyin yi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyin, the prefectural seat county.

sentences.zh: 有曹南山、定濮岡、左山、祝丘、荷水、氾水、饗城、鄸城。

translations.literal: There are Mount Cao South, Dingpu Mound, Mount Zuo, Zhuxiu, He River, Fan River, Xiangcheng, and Zhengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: It had Mount Cao South, Dingpu Mound, Mount Zuo, Zhuxiu, the He and Fan rivers, Xiangcheng, and Zhengcheng.

translations.literal: One town: Pushui.
translations.idiomatic: One town: Pushui.

sentences.zh: 定陶本宋廣濟軍，熙寧間廢為定陶縣。

translations.literal: Dingtao was originally the Song Guangji Army; between the Xining era it was abolished and made Dingtao county.
translations.idiomatic: Dingtao had been the Song Guangji Army; in the Xining period it was abolished and became Dingtao county.

translations.literal: Within the city is the Terrace of the King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city stood the Terrace of the King of Liang.

translations.literal: There are Mount Fang and Mount Dugu.
translations.idiomatic: It had Mount Fang and Mount Dugu.

sentences.zh: 東明初隸南京，後避河患，徙河北冤句故地。

translations.literal: Dongming was at first subordinate to Nanjing; later, to escape river damage, it moved to the old Yuanqu land north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Dongming had first been under Nanjing; later, fleeing flood harm, it shifted to old Yuanqu territory north of the river.

sentences.zh: 後以故縣為蘭陽、儀封，有舊東明城。

translations.literal: Later the old county became Lanyang and Yifeng; there remains the old Dongming city.
translations.idiomatic: Later the former county seat was divided into Lanyang and Yifeng, and the old Dongming city still stood.
